newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip on profit-taking, U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip on profit-taking, U.S. holiday.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased on Thursday on profit-taking, mainly in the fourth tranche, and ahead of the long Labour Day weekend in the U.S., dealers said.
They added trading was otherwise uncertain and thin on fears Russian police may freeze up to a further $7 million nominal of MinFin bonds which have been stolen.
"Some banks are still not trading as they do not want to take the risk. The rest are quoting prices but they seem reluctant to work actively," one dealer said.

Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said: "There has been a little drop mainly for two reasons, position-squaring ahead of a longer U.S. weekend and because somebody has made nice profits selling the fourth tranche."
He added a trend of narrowing the gap between the 2008 and 2006 maturities has appeared, with operators mainly selling the latter and buying the former.
